artboards.title: The row, and what a reading does to it

annotations.text:
A STOCK ROOM, NOT A STOCK MARKET
rp_corporations.stock is how much a corporation is HOLDING, and nobody buys a share. So falling is the opportunity: stores draining means they are consuming, which means they will pay for a haul.

That inverts the convention the shape borrows, so the palette went with it. Red is gone entirely — there is no bad news for someone with a cart full of ore — and $phone-pink means one thing only: they are buying. A restocked corporation goes quiet instead.

EYEBROWS FOLLOW THE CONVENTION
The two headers on the watchlist are .phone-section-label to the letter — 10px, 1px tracking, uppercase, --ph-faint, 18px of air above and 6px beneath, the first one dropping its top margin because the header supplies that air, and the group below contributing no top gap of its own.

The 8.5px labels in the stats strip are a different vocabulary again - the meta strip from the App Store's app page - and are not eyebrows.

Grouping the list under those two headers also retired the "most room first" subtitle — the eyebrows say it better than a sentence did.

CAPACITY IS THE NEW COLUMN
stock_capacity does not exist yet — this design asks for it. Without it a farmer cannot tell whether 302 is low, and the whole app rests on that judgement.

With it, every row carries a bar at its foot: how full they are, at a glance, down the column. Below half full it turns pink — that is the threshold where a haul is worth carrying. The corporation page then says it in words, "under a third full, room for 658", which is the sentence the reader was trying to form.

SORTED BY ROOM, NOT MOVEMENT
You said sort by movement, and that was right when the number was all we had. Capacity beats it: "who can take my haul" is answered by how empty they are, not by who twitched most. So fullness leads and the chip still carries direction — a corporation can be nearly full and draining fast, and you can see both.

Easy to flip back if you would rather movement led.

TWO CLOCKS, ONE ALWAYS OFF
• The LEDGER samples every 10 minutes server-side. That is the history: five rows every ten minutes, ~65k across three months.
• The APP asks on open, then every 60s while it stays open, and NOTHING while the phone is shut.

Stock only moves when a player sells, so anything finer is sampling silence. Ranges stop at 3M because a nightly purge keeps only 90 days — 1D is 144 samples and arrives whole — that is the range players sit on, so it is deliberately never thinned. 3M is ~13,000 and is strided to 144 evenly spaced points on the server first.

WHAT THIS NEEDS FROM THE SERVER
• stock_capacity on rp_corporations — an int beside stock. Everything on these boards that says "full" depends on it.
• A samples table: corporation, value, timestamp. Written every 10 minutes, purged past 90 days. BUILT.
• One packet the app can ask for: current values plus a window of samples.

All three are built and on beta, along with :setstock <acronym> <quantity> for staff — nothing in the game writes stock yet, so that is how the number moves until farming and mining land.
